page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton generation 8 arm64 processors. The instance delivers 192 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, with a single-thread-per-core configuration that avoids simultaneous multithreading contention. It is provisioned with 1536.0 GB of system memory, translating to a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server contains no integrated GPUs.

Storage and networking configurations prioritize network bandwidth over local storage devices. The system contains no onboard local drive storage, requiring data persistence to be handled over the network via Amazon Elastic Block Store. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 600 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data ingestion and node synchronization across large clusters. Direct bare-metal access removes hypervisor overhead, though workloads must be compatible with the arm64 instruction set.

The 1.5 TB memory footprint and 192 dedicated cores offer high compute and memory density within an arm64 architecture. The server is suited for memory-bound applications, including large-scale in-memory databases, massive caching deployments, distributed data processing engines, and high-throughput enterprise pipelines.

The server does not contain dedicated GPUs or onboard local storage, depending entirely on networked block storage for persistent data needs. The r8gn.metal-48xl provides high resource density and operational efficiency on custom ARM silicon, making it well matched for in-memory databases, large cache layers, distributed data analytics engines, and enterprise memory-intensive workloads that require massive RAM and dedicated compute without local disk drives.
